"Instead of burning or shredding garden prunings this winter, repurpose them into a dead hedge. This can act as a windbreak, provide refuge for wildlife, and divide areas of your garden. Construct the hedge by planting stakes or old fence posts in two rows, 50 cm apart, and slot the prunings in between, with larger branches at the base. As the material settles over time, the hedge will take shape.

If you didn't receive any impressive gifts this Christmas, cheer yourself up by pre-ordering a copy of 'The Book Of Seeds' by Paul Smith, former head of Kew's Millennium Seed Bank. This guide, published in February, showcases 600 of the world's most peculiar and beautiful seed species, from the black seed with hair like Donald Trump to pinhead-sized orchid seeds.

Winter-flowering clematis is a sight to behold. If you can offer it a sunny, sheltered spot, you'll be rewarded with blooms from December to February. Clematis cirrhosa 'Advent Bells' (3m x 1.5m) and C. cirrhosa var. balearica (2.5m x 1.5m) both have creamy, scented flowers with maroon splashes, while C. cirrhosa 'Jingle Bells' has pure white blooms and reaches 5m x 2m."
